newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Chase Manhattan denies reports on Romania loan.
newsitem.headline: Chase Manhattan denies reports on Romania loan.

text.p: The Romanian branch of Chase Manhattan denied on Friday local media reports saying the bank had suspended talks with the state-run National Oil Company (CRP) on a $200 million credit to finance vital crude oil imports for Romania during the coming winter.
Last winter, an acute shortage of hard currency cut Romania's oil imports. The Balkan country was forced to cut electricity supplies drastically to its main industries.
"The deal is not in any way affected at this point," a bank official told Reuters.
On Friday, several local newspapers said Chase Manhattan and CRP negotiations were halted, pending clarification of a Court of Appeal ruling to dissolve the oil giant.

"No, those reports are not correct. We continue to work on the deal and to talk to CRP on the assumption clarification is forthcoming," the official said, adding that the bank had asked the CRP to clarify the suspension issue by mid-December.

On Tuesday, the Court of Appeal ruled to suspend the CRP after a local private firm, General Trading and Investments Co SA (GTI), filed a lawsuit accusing the state-run holding of monopolistic practices. GTI asked the court to annul the government decision last July that created the CRP.

CRP officials have denied GTI's charges and threatened to sue the company for slander and damages. The holding, which groups 12 state-owned refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies and an oil exploration company, would appeal to the Supreme Court, they said.
"As regards suing for damages, our position is naturally that such course of action would not be successful and would be a waste of public money," GTI's Ian Deacon told Reuters.
"Any consequences of our actions and proposals can only increase the efficiency and profitability and therefore, the value of the industry and those parts of it which constitute CRP," he said.
GTI also complained in court that CRP had hindered its oil imports by blocking access to the country's sole oil port, Constanta on the Black Sea.
CRP general manager Mihail Georgescu told Reuters on Friday that GTI's allegations were groundless.
Georgescu accused GTI of "completely" failing to fulfill a contract to import and process 780,000 tonnes of crude oil in CRP's refineries over the past six months.
"They were not able to bring a single drop of crude in those six months," Georgescu said. "So how come we've hindered their operation? Where is the oil?
"They had to pay a $1 million fine for not fulfilling the contract, and this was irritating."
Georgescu also said CRP data showed last year GTI imported and processed 230,000 tonnes of crude, which he said was less than half the quantity agreed to in a 1995 contract.
